metadata.title: MAPP 4200.3 Rev.2 Consulting the Controlled Substance Staff on Abuse Liability, Drug Dependence, Risk Management, and Drug Scheduling
metadata.legal_basis: CDER Manual of Policies and Procedures (internal FDA review procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.
metadata.applicability: FDA staff procedure. Category: Drug Safety.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: 1. CSS performs the abuse potential, dependence liability, and drug scheduling assessments for CDER. CSS evaluates drugs and other substances submitted under INDs, NDAs, and BLAs that have effects on the central nervous system (CNS) and need to be assessed for the extent to which the drug has a stimulant, depressant, or hallucinogenic effect. Examples include those drugs classified as known opioids, stimulants, hallucinogens, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, cannabinoids or those classified as anabolic steroids, but also includes CNS-active new molecular entities that may prove to have similar drug effects. These drugs must be evaluated for abuse potential as part of the overall assessment of the drug’s safety. Contact CSS if there is uncertainty about the need for a formal consultation.
candidates.context: 2. All CDER Offices and Divisions are required to consult CSS to evaluate drugs from an abuse perspective during the review of investigational new drug applications (INDs), new drug applications (NDAs), biological licensing agreements (BLAs) that meet the criteria listed in item 1. Under rare circumstances, CSS evaluates abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs), as described in item 8.

candidates.statement: 5. For NDA and BLA submissions, applicants are required to submit and summarize all abuse- and dependence-related information collected during IND development
candidates.context: c. Clinical and nonclinical physical dependence studies. Effective Date: 05/08/03; 3/6/17 ; 10/26/22 Page 2 of 8

candidates.statement: 7. CSS reviews products formulated to have abuse-deterrence, and should be consulted to review protocols or resulting data for studies investigating abuse- deterrent properties and proposed labeling claims.
candidates.context: 6. For some NDA and BLA submissions, CSS conducts additional scientific and medical evaluations [Eight-Factor Analyses, see 21 U.S.C. 811(b) and (c)] to determine if a drug warrants control under the CSA and thus requires the preparation of a scheduling recommendation. When necessary after review of the information submitted, CSS drafts a scheduling recommendation in parallel with a CSS review of the NDA. This recommendation is transmitted to the DEA. CSS makes recommendations on labeling to the consulting Office/Division consistent with the scheduling recommendation and the drug’s abuse and dependence liabilities. 8. Under rare circumstances, the Office of Generic Drugs (OGD) consults CSS.

candidates.statement: Instances include when an ANDA involves a drug product for which a new scheduling recommendation is necessary. OGD may also need to consult CSS for generic products referencing a reference listed drug (RLD) for an abuse-deterrent opioid product, e.g., when clinical studies were conducted to demonstrate that the generic opioid drug product is no less abuse-deterrent than the RLD.
candidates.context: 8. Under rare circumstances, the Office of Generic Drugs (OGD) consults CSS. 9. After concurrence between CSS and the consulting Division, CSS’s advice and recommendations to sponsors are conveyed by the consulting CDER Office or Division. Following the procedures outlined in MAPP 6030.9, Good Review Practice: Good Review Management Principles and Practices for Effective IND Development and Review , the review divisions consult CSS at major milestones in drug development.

candidates.statement: 5. Informs IND sponsors and NDA or BLA applicants that information and communication related to abuse, misuse, substance use disorder, diversion, dependence, and abuse deterrence must be submitted to the regulatory file.
candidates.context: CSS generally needs 30 days to prepare for industry meetings, to perform IND reviews, and to prepare for filing meetings. CSS will endeavor to meet Division timelines by providing input in less than 30 days in necessary cases, for example IND safety review meetings. Consultations on NDAs, PMR study reports, abuse- related protocols and abuse-related risk management issues require longer preparation times. For example, for NDA submissions reviewed under PDUFA timelines, the CSS reviewer will review the NDA under the same timelines as all other subject matter disciplines. 6. Consults CSS for input and clearance, as appropriate, when drafting abuse potential-related advice sections of sponsor communications.

candidates.statement: a. A consult request for NDA or BLA evaluations should occur promptly upon receipt of the NDA or BLA, as the CSS reviewer will review the NDA under the same timelines as all other subject matter disciplines and participates in the filing review.
candidates.context: 1. CDER office or division completes the general consult request form (FRM - CONSULT-01). b. All other consult requests should be submitted as soon as possible and by a date that allows adequate time for the requested review.
